q: Which labels fit my Rollo or Zebra printer?
a: Rollo printers take 4 x 6 direct thermal fanfold or 1-inch core rolls. Zebra desktop printers (GK420d, ZD410/ZD421, LP2844) take the same plus 2 x 1 and 2.25 x 1.25 rolls on 1-inch cores; Zebra industrial printers also take 3-inch cores. Every product page lists compatible printers, or use the printer finder.

q: What is the difference between direct thermal and thermal transfer?
a: Direct thermal labels darken with heat, so no ribbon is needed - perfect for shipping labels. Thermal transfer labels are printed through a ribbon, so the image lasts for years and resists heat and abrasion - better for inventory and product barcodes.
The core is the cardboard tube in the middle of a roll. Desktop printers use 1-inch cores; industrial printers use 3-inch cores. Fanfold and sheet labels have no core.

q: Should I choose fanfold or rolls?
a: Fanfold stacks sit behind the printer and feed continuously, so they hold more labels and need no spindle - great for Rollo and other high-volume desktop printers. Rolls suit printers with an internal spindle, such as the Dymo 4XL.
